specPoints.text: be able to define the terms ‘enthalpy change of solution, ∆ sol H ’ and ‘ enthalpy change of hydration , ∆ hyd H of an ion’

primer.text: Dissolving an ionic solid has two energetic faces: the endothermic breakdown of the lattice and the exothermic hydration of its ions. This note defines the enthalpy of solution and the enthalpy of hydration, writes their equations with state symbols, and shows how polar water molecules bind ions through ion-dipole attractions.

lessons.title: Solution and hydration enthalpies
lessons.opening: Two definitions run the whole solution-energetics topic. The enthalpy of solution covers one mole of solid dissolving into infinitely dilute solution - exothermic or endothermic, compound by compound. The enthalpy of hydration covers one mole of gaseous ions entering water - always exothermic, because ion-dipole attractions form as polar water molecules wrap the ions.
keyPoints: The standard enthalpy change of solution (delta sol H): the enthalpy change that results when enough water dissolves 1 mole of an ionic substance to make an infinitely dilute solution.
The (aq) symbol records dissolution in sufficient water; for potassium chloride: KCl (s) plus aq forming KCl (aq), or as separated ions K+ (aq) and Cl- (aq).
Delta sol H can be exothermic (negative) or endothermic (positive), depending on the compound.

The standard enthalpy change of hydration (delta hyd H): the enthalpy change that results when 1 mole of a stated gaseous ion enters water to give an infinitely dilute solution, as in Mg2+ (g) plus aq forming Mg2+ (aq).
Hydration enthalpies are exothermic: energy is released as attractions form between the ions and water molecules.
Water is polar, with a delta-negative oxygen and delta-positive hydrogens, so ion-dipole attractions form: oxygen faces positive ions and hydrogens face negative ions.

low.restatement: Solution enthalpy: solid plus aq, either sign. Hydration enthalpy: gaseous ion plus aq, always negative, thanks to ion-dipole attractions.
low.analogy: Moving house (dissolving) versus settling into a furnished flat (hydrating): the first may cost or gain, the second always furnishes warmth.
low.examPointer: Write the state symbols aq and g exactly - definitions are graded on them.

medium.restatement: Dissolution has two faces - break the lattice, then let water embrace each ion - and hydration is the embracing term, always releasing energy because new attractions form.
medium.analogy: Undoing a packing crate (lattice) and then arranging each item on a shelf that fits it (hydration).
medium.examPointer: The 'infinitely dilute' phrase guards against ion-ion interactions - quote it in definitions.

check.stem: The standard enthalpy change of solution is defined per

options.text: 1 mole of ionic substance dissolving in enough water to make an infinitely dilute solution
options.explanation: One mole, sufficient water, infinite dilution.

options.text: 1 mole of gaseous ions entering water
1 mole of lattice breaking into gaseous ions
Any amount dissolving in a fixed beaker
options.explanation: The definition fixes one mole and infinite dilution.

check.stem: The enthalpy of solution for a compound can be

options.text: Either exothermic or endothermic, depending on the compound
options.explanation: The balance of lattice and hydration terms decides.

check.stem: The enthalpy of hydration is always exothermic because

options.text: Attractions form between the gaseous ion and the polar water molecules

options.explanation: The ion keeps its charge in solution.
Lattice breaking belongs to the solution side.

check.stem: In the ion-dipole picture, the oxygen atom of water faces

options.text: Positive ions, since the oxygen carries the delta-negative charge

check.stem: The hydration equation for magnesium ions is

options.text: Mg2+ (g) plus aq forming Mg2+ (aq), exothermic
options.explanation: Gaseous ion in, aqueous ion out, energy out.
The definition starts from the gaseous ion.

options.text: MgCl2 (s) plus aq forming Mg2+ (aq) plus 2Cl- (aq)
options.explanation: That is a solution enthalpy, not hydration.

check.stem: State the enthalpy of solution equation for potassium chloride.
check.modelAnswer: KCl (s) plus aq forming KCl (aq), or K+ (aq) plus Cl- (aq) after separation.

check.stem: State the sign and cause of hydration enthalpies.
check.modelAnswer: Always exothermic, caused by attractions forming between the gaseous ion and polar water molecules.

check.stem: Explain why the gaseous ion is the starting point of the hydration definition.
check.modelAnswer: Defining from the gaseous ion isolates the ion-water interaction alone; starting from a solid would bundle lattice breaking into the measurement, mixing two separate energetic events.

check.stem: A compound's dissolving feels cold to the touch. State its solution enthalpy sign and identify the exothermic partner process that partly offsets the lattice cost.
check.modelAnswer: The solution enthalpy is positive (endothermic), and the hydration of its ions is the exothermic partner that repays part of the lattice-breaking cost.

glossary.definition: The enthalpy change when 1 mole of ionic substance dissolves in enough water to make an infinitely dilute solution.
The enthalpy change when 1 mole of gaseous ion dissolves in water to form an infinitely dilute solution; always exothermic.
The attraction between an ion and the delta charges of polar water molecules.
